sections.title: Why creativity alone is not enough

items.q: What shocked Po-Shen Loh about AI and the Math Olympiad?
items.a: Google's AI solved **4 of 6** International Math Olympiad problems — questions coaches verify as globally original. Loh says **AI creativity may surpass ours too**; hoping humans still exist is not a skill strategy.

items.q: What skill does he actually hire and coach for?
items.a: **Synthesis on novel problems**: wait until body language shows a student has **never seen** the problem, give hints, and measure how fast they **synthesize** a solution. That edge matters more than raw creativity claims.

items.q: Why is using AI for school writing homework so damaging?
items.a: It is like **driving your car one mile for exercise** — zero mental fitness. School writing is **learning**, not job output. Adults can use AI at work; students who outsource language become **dependent thinkers** who cannot evaluate what others hand them.

items.q: How should pedagogy shift in an LLM world?
items.a: Learn to **grade homework**, not just do it. School tests reward listening plus practice; the world needs large-scale training in **creative thinking on novel problems** and verification of AI outputs.

items.q: What did coaching the US IMO team teach him about competition?
items.a: Brilliant, capable people were still **depressed** when life meant proving you are better than others. He replaces outdoing with **make others happy** — addictive at scale from 5 → 500 → 1,000 people.

items.q: What becomes a survival skill once humans are not the top species?
items.a: **Delight others to survive AGI**: you must team up; the only way others partner with you is authentic motivation to **create value in them**. Bad partners get excluded and lose opportunity.

items.q: How does efficient AI use steal more than productivity?
items.a: It can erase **personal taste** (fashion, ideas) and, without reasoning ability, leave you open to **agenda-driven narratives**. 2+2=4 is settled; the point of life has no single answer.

items.q: Why should you not trust one AI provider for the full story?
items.a: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek are roughly **5 curated worldviews** vs **7.5 billion**. Loh reads CNN + Fox and tunes opposing feeds daily so AI's complete-sounding answers do not hide one-sided framing.

items.q: What surprised him in rural high-poverty classrooms?
items.a: Fourth graders **without phones or internet** yelled math ideas respectfully and invented their own games — **digital absence** unlocked authentic curiosity and untapped science/tech potential.

items.q: What philosophy does he want kids to keep as AI makes thinking optional?
items.a: **It's fun to think** — life's fun is your own contribution and twist, not AI-efficient outsourcing. iPad entertainment erodes concentration; synthesis skill matters most when university itself may look different by the time kids enroll.
